answer.summary: Usable food-service days after losing a major channel remain unknown for Alameda County. ACCFB's published 2025 response demonstrates a surge mechanism, not a current stock buffer: it reports procurement increases and emergency distributions. Its 2026 agenda identifies added demand pressure, while the current help page offers a same-day referral pathway. The next useful measurement is dated accessible stock and confirmed replenishment against daily need at one distribution point.
counterevidence: ACCFB reports having expanded procurement and launched pop-up distributions in 2025; lost benefits do not imply that all replacement channels fail.
A currently published referral service is evidence of an access pathway, although not evidence of fulfilled meals or spare capacity.
limitations: Three primary pages from one organization; no independent corroboration or live service test.
Historical surge response is not September 2026 operating capacity. No stock, daily demand, current unrestricted cash, staffed throughput or confirmed incoming loads was established.
Benefit loss is household purchasing-power loss, not itself a missing food-bank shipment. Its effect on pantry demand is a plausible interacting stress, not a measured demand increment here.
No inference that fuel prices have caused missed food deliveries. Repository feed leads do not measure fulfillment.
No new canonical answer admitted; Work review pending.

conditional_link.stress: Loss of household food-purchasing support or a food-bank supply channel
conditional_link.mechanism: More households may seek pantry food while usable inflows or purchasing capacity fail to keep pace. Transport, staffing and access can bind before warehouse stocks run out.
conditional_link.confirmation: At one named site, obtain a dated public report of usable inventory, daily household demand, confirmed arrival dates and documented shortfalls attributable to the lost channel; compare cover with replenishment lead time.
conditional_link.falsification: For that site and interval, independently financed replacement arrivals plus accessible stock and staffed distribution meet demand without missed service; benefit or fuel changes alone do not activate the proposed link.
conditional_link.time_horizon: Daily service and next replenishment; no run-out date calculated.

resilience.buffers: Candidate: rotating usable staples and confirmed purchased replenishment. Actual quantities, funding and cover are unknown.
resilience.safe_shedding: Proposal: reduce duplicated collection trips and optional handling, not meal adequacy or access for people unable to travel; avoid concentrating pickups into inaccessible windows.
resilience.adaptation_growth: Proposal: build a small shared pickup/return-container routine, then expand only after a provider confirms supply, staffing, safe handling and receiving capacity.
resilience.lifeboat: Published ACCFB helpline offers same-day food-provider connection during weekday business hours; actual food availability, travel access and after-hours fallback remain unverified.
resilience.outside_donor_capacity: Unknown. Count only dated, compatible surplus after the donor's existing commitments and contingency floor, with transport and receiving staff confirmed.
resilience.commons: Proposal: a one-page, opt-in food-access board showing last-verified opening times, next pickup, transport need and a backup provider. No beneficiary names or sensitive details; no partner or volunteer commitment is claimed.

caretaker.actor: ACCFB publishes the referral pathway; a specific receiving provider is not yet verified.
caretaker.authority: Published service remit, not an emergency guarantee.
caretaker.trigger: A food-help request; any surge activation trigger is unknown.
caretaker.response_time: Published same-day referral during listed helpline hours; actual fulfillment time unknown.
caretaker.tomorrow_test: Can one identified site verify an accessible food handoff tomorrow, with quantity, hours, transport and a fallback if its expected load does not arrive?

sample_for_jared.title: A bridge is not the same as a pantry
sample_for_jared.original: Clearly hypothetical: a pantry holds 240 usable household food packages and needs 80 per day. With no new arrivals, stock-only cover is three days. If transport cannot reach it, accessible cover may be lower.
sample_for_jared.english_pivot: The important question is not just 'Is there food?' but 'Can people actually receive it before the next load?'
sample_for_jared.control: Clearly hypothetical ordinary case: confirmed replenishment arrives on day two and distribution continues normally. A larger procurement bill alone does not establish a shortage.
sample_for_jared.translation_note: No multilingual pair was inspected in this food-cover session. Jared's language selections remain open; grammar, idiom, space, timing and translator habit remain ordinary explanations to test in a future matched comparison.

reflection.summary: A demonstrated emergency response and a published access pathway are useful bridges, but neither supplies the missing denominator for days of food cover.
observations: The 2025 response provides counterevidence to an assumption of helplessness without proving spare capacity today.
The missing measurement is usable food in reachable service, not merely an organization's existence or a larger purchasing percentage.
Three pages from one organization supply different kinds of evidence, not three independent confirmations.
suggestions: Keep stock, throughput, referral and fulfilled service as separate fields.
Use a small capacity card at one site before enlarging the research network.
questions: What is the smallest public operational record that could establish reachable food cover and next replenishment for one East Bay site?
uncertainties: Current inventory, demand, cash, transport and donor floor remain unknown.

governor_response.summary: Explore the scouts' missing operating-capacity denominator through Q17, acknowledge unchanged feed retrieval without treating repetition as corroboration, and retain the provider brake. The food-bank comparison shows useful reflection changing the next evidence target. Rhetorical framing is separate from the service claims tested here; no silent beliefs or translation mismatch are inferred.

followups.question: Review this provisional Q17 packet; retain historical surge capability separately from unknown current service cover.
Within a later bounded session, can one public site-level record establish usable stock, daily service demand and the next confirmed delivery without contacting anyone?

governor_response.self_reflection: A helpful finding can be a demonstrated bridge plus a precise missing measurement. Reflection should change the next check, not inflate uncertainty into a collapse claim.
